Latin word

sevērus

sevērus, sevēra, sevērum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

serious, grave, stern (of a person or a face); strict, stern, grave

In this lexicon

  • serious

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.228: omnium gravissimus et sevērissimus (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 2.289: vultus sevērior et trīstior (Lewis & Short)

  • severe

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Heaut. 1023: quam sevērus!; Cic. Lael. 95: cīvis sevērus et gravis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158, 146; Traupman 326

  • sevērus et gravis: formal

    classical

Examples

  • Sed ipse ēgreditur: quam sevērus!

    But here he comes out himself: how stern he looks!Ter. Heaut. 1023

    In the entry for severe

  • Nōn possum: satis jam satis pater dūrus fuī.

    I can’t: I have been a harsh father long enough, more than enough.Ter. Heaut. 439
